```{r 03}
# Two changes that we agreed on in the workshop/meetings: 
data_original <- 
  data_original %>% 
  rename(measurement_id = row_id, 
         control_id = comparison_id)

data_original <- 
  data_original %>% 
  group_by(reference) %>%
  mutate(
    study_id = ifelse(ma_id == "D1120", cur_group_id(), study_id),
    control_id = ifelse(ma_id == "D1120", row_number(), control_id)
  ) %>%

# reverse the whole D352 because its coordinates are switched
data_original <- 
  data_original %>% 
  mutate(
    temp = ifelse(ma_id == "D352", longitude, NA_real_),  # Temporarily store Long in temp
    longitude = ifelse(ma_id == "D352", latitude, longitude),  # Replace Long with Lat

  ) %>%
  select(-temp)
```

### 1.1. Assign coordinate format

Here we loose 138 observations because they have NAs in lat or long.
1.10.24 added a comma to the dot so that we can define both delimeter formats

```{r 11}
df <- data_original %>%
  filter(!(longitude %in% NA_character_)) %>% 
  filter(!(latitude %in% NA_character_)) %>%
  mutate(long_coordinate_format = case_when(
    str_detect(longitude, "^[\\+-]?((1[0-7]\\d|[1-9]?\\d)([\\.,]\\d{1,})?|180)\\D*[EWew]?$") ~ "DD",
    str_detect(longitude, "^[\\+-]?((1[0-7]\\d|[1-9]?\\d)\\D+[0-6]?\\d([\\.,]\\d{1,})?|180(\\D+0)?)\\D+[EWew]?$") ~ "DDM",
    str_detect(longitude, "^[\\+-]?([1-7]?\\d{1,2}\\D+([0-5]?\\d|60)\\D+([0-5]?\\d|60)([\\.,]\\d+)?|180\\D+0\\D+0)\\D+[EWew]?$") ~ "DMS",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>% 
  mutate(lat_coordinate_format = case_when(
    str_detect(latitude, "^[\\+-]?(([1-8]?\\d)([\\.,]\\d{1,})?([\\.,]\\d{1,})?|90)\\D*[NSns]?$") ~ "DD",
    str_detect(latitude, "^[\\+-]?(([1-8]?\\d)\\D+[0-6]?\\d([\\.,]\\d{1,})?|90(\\D+0)?)\\D+[NSns]?$") ~ "DDM",
    str_detect(latitude, "^[\\+-]?(([1-8]?\\d)\\D+([0-5]?\\d|60)\\D+([0-5]?\\d|60)([\\.,]\\d+)?|90\\D+0\\D+0)\\D+[NSns]?$") ~ "DMS",
    
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>% 
  mutate(long_coordinate_format = if_else(
    long_coordinate_format %in% NA_character_, 
    case_when(
      str_detect(longitude, "^[\\+-]?((1[0-7]\\d|[1-9]?\\d)\\D+[0-6]?\\d([\\.,]\\d{1,})?|180(\\D+0)?)\\D+[EWew]?-[\\+-]?((1[0-7]\\d|[0-9]?\\d)\\D+[0-6]?\\d([\\.,]\\d{1,})?|180(\\D+0)?)\\D+[EWew]?$"
      ) ~ "DDM interval"
    ), long_coordinate_format
  )) %>% 
  mutate(lat_coordinate_format = if_else(
    lat_coordinate_format %in% NA_character_, 
    case_when(
      str_detect(latitude, "^[\\+-]?(([1-8]?\\d)\\D+[0-6]?\\d([\\.,]\\d{1,})?|90(\\D+0)?)\\D+[NSns]?-[\\+-]?(([1-8]?\\d)\\D+[0-6]?\\d([\\.,]\\d{1,})?|90(\\D+0)?)\\D+[NSns]?$"
      ) ~ "DDM interval"
    ), lat_coordinate_format
  )) %>% 
  mutate(long_coordinate_format =  as.factor(long_coordinate_format),
         lat_coordinate_format =  as.factor(lat_coordinate_format))
```

Total Observations: 10232

### 1.2. Shorten the DDM intervals for decimal conversio

```{r 12}
df <- 
  df %>% 
  filter(!(long_coordinate_format %in% NA_character_),
         !(lat_coordinate_format %in% NA_character_)) %>% 
  mutate(longitude_temp = case_when(
    long_coordinate_format == "DDM interval" ~ str_extract(longitude, "^[^-]+"), # extracts everything before the dash 
    TRUE ~ longitude
  )) %>% 
  mutate(latitude_temp = case_when(
    lat_coordinate_format == "DDM interval"~ str_extract(latitude, "^[^-]+"),
    TRUE ~ latitude
  )) 
```

### 2. Convert coordinate to decimals

### 2.1. Replace all nondigits with semicolon

```{r 21}
replace_nondigits <- function(string) {
  # Remove leading "-" if present
  string <- str_replace(string, "^-", "")
  
  # Remove all letters
  string <- str_remove_all(string, "[A-Za-z]")
  
  # Remove whitespaces
  string <- str_replace(string, " ", "")
  
  
  # Replace remaining non-digit characters except for "." with ";"
  new_string <- gsub("[^0-9\\.]", ";", string)
  
  # Replace ";;" with ";"
  result_string <- gsub(";;", ";", new_string)
  
  return(result_string)
}


replace_nondigits_vector <- function(strings) {
  new_strings <- lapply(strings, replace_nondigits)
  return(new_strings)
}
```

### 2.2. Extract all digits and divide them into three groups

```{r 22}
# first = degreesm, second = minutes, third = seconds 

extract_digits_from_string <- function(string) {
  # Split the string into parts based on semicolons
  parts <- strsplit(string, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  
  # Extract digits and dots from each part
  first <- gsub("[^0-9\\.]", "", parts[1])
  second <- ifelse(length(parts) >= 2, gsub("[^0-9\\.]", "", parts[2]), 0)
  third <- ifelse(length(parts) >= 3, gsub("[^0-9\\.]", "", parts[3]), 0)
  
  # Replace NA values with 0
  first <- ifelse(is.na(first), 0, first)
  second <- ifelse(is.na(second), 0, second)
  third <- ifelse(is.na(third), 0, third)
  
  # Return the extracted digits as a list
  return(list(first = first, second = second, third = third))
}

extract_digits_from_vector <- function(strings) {
  results <- lapply(strings, extract_digits_from_string)
  return(results)
}
```

### 2.3. Apply the replace and extract functions

```{r 23}
df <- 
  df %>% 
  mutate(
    longitudecomma = sapply(longitude_temp, replace_nondigits_vector),
    latitudecomma = sapply(latitude_temp, replace_nondigits_vector)
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    longitudedigits = sapply(longitudecomma, extract_digits_from_vector),
    latitudedigits = sapply(latitudecomma, extract_digits_from_vector)
  ) 
```

Total Observations: 9972

### 2.4. Calculate the decimal degrees

```{r 24}
df <- 
  df %>%
  mutate(
    longitudedigits = purrr::map(longitudedigits, unlist), 
    latitudedigits = purrr::map(latitudedigits, unlist)
  ) %>%
  unnest_wider(col = c(longitudedigits, latitudedigits), names_sep = "_") %>%
  mutate(across(longitudedigits_first:latitudedigits_third, as.numeric)) %>% 
  mutate(
    longitude_DD = longitudedigits_first + longitudedigits_second / 60 + longitudedigits_third / 3600,
    latitude_DD = latitudedigits_first + latitudedigits_second / 60 + latitudedigits_third / 3600
  ) 
```

Total Observations: 9972

### 2.5. Extract direction and dimension of the coordinates

```{r 25}
extract_direction_and_dimension <- function(df, longitude_col, latitude_col) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      longitude_direction = case_when(
        str_detect(!!sym(longitude_col), "[SsWw]") | str_starts(!!sym(longitude_col), "^-") ~ "-",
        TRUE ~ "+"
      ),
      latitude_direction = case_when(
        str_detect(!!sym(latitude_col), "[SsWw]") | str_starts(!!sym(latitude_col), "^-") ~ "-",
        TRUE ~ "+"
      )
    )
}

# extract it:
df<- 
  df %>%
  extract_direction_and_dimension("longitude", "latitude")

```

### 2.6. Apply the extracted directions to the decomal degrees

```{r 26}
apply_direction_to_coordinates <- function(df, longitude_col, latitude_col) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      longitude_DD_direction = ifelse(longitude_direction == "-", -longitude_DD, longitude_DD),
      latitude_DD_direction = ifelse(latitude_direction == "-", -latitude_DD, latitude_DD)
    )
}

df <- apply_direction_to_coordinates(df, "longitude_DD", "latitude_DD")

```

```{r 27}
df <-
```

### 3.1 Assign country_new based on DD coordinates

```{r 31}

maptomap <- getMap(resolution = "high")


coords2country <- function(df, longitude_col, latitude_col) {
  # Get country polygons
  countriesSP <- getMap(resolution = "high")
  
  # Create SpatialPoints object from df frame
  pointsSP <- SpatialPoints(df[, c(longitude_col, latitude_col)], proj4string = CRS(proj4string(countriesSP)))
  
  # Overlap points with countries to get country names
  countries <- over(pointsSP, countriesSP)
  
  # Add country names to the df frame
  df$country_new <- countries$ADMIN
  
  return(df)
}

df <- coords2country(df, "longitude_decimal", "latitude_decimal")
```

### 5. Calculate the land cover map year

### 5.1. Add missing publication years per hand

```{r 51}
df_pubyear_added <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\lisa7\\Documents\\surrounding_landscapes\\my_computer_files\\df_pubyear_added.csv")  
df_pubyear_added <- 
  df_pubyear_added %>% 
  select(row_id, study_pubyear) 

df <- 
  left_join(df, df_pubyear_added, join_by("measurement_id"=="row_id") )

df <- 
  df %>% 
  mutate(
    study_pubyear.x = ifelse(study_pubyear.x %in% NA_character_, study_pubyear.y, study_pubyear.x)) 

df <- 
  df %>% 
  select(-study_pubyear.y) %>% 
  rename(study_pubyear = study_pubyear.x) %>% 
  mutate(across(study_pubyear, as.numeric)) # here you set the "unpublished" studies to NA

rm(df_pubyear_added)
```

#### Add D652

D652 saved its publication year and titles in a separate word document.
So, it has to be added to our dataset.

```{r 52}
df_d652 <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\lisa7\\Documents\\surrounding_landscapes\\my_computer_files\\d652_years.csv", header = FALSE)  
df_d652 <-
  df_d652 %>%
  rename(`ma_id` = `V1`,
         `study_id` = `V2`,
         `reference` = `V3`) %>% 
  select(-V4) 

df_d652 <-
  df_d652 %>% 
  mutate(study_pubyear = str_extract(df_d652$reference, 
                                     "\\b(19[6-9][0-9]|20[0-1][0-9]|2020|2021|2022)\\b") 
         # in this case the Year extraction is kind of awkward because the source 
         # utilized different citation styles, 
         # and I cannot extract just the 4 digits or define the surroundings.
  ) %>% 
  mutate(ma_id_study_id = paste0("D652", sep = "_", as.character(study_id))) %>% 
  select(ma_id_study_id, study_pubyear, reference) %>% 
  unique()  %>% 
  mutate(across(study_pubyear, as.numeric))

df_d652 <- 
  df_d652 %>% 
  mutate(study_pubyear = case_when(
    ma_id_study_id == "D652_238" ~ 2011, # reason added: code glitch. year present in the csv
    TRUE ~ study_pubyear 
  ))

```

### 5.3. Merge df with D652

```{r 53}

df <- 
  df %>%

df <-   
  left_join(df, df_d652, join_by("ma_id_study_id"=="ma_id_study_id"),

df <- 
  df %>% 
  mutate(study_pubyear.x = ifelse(ma_id == "D652", study_pubyear.y, study_pubyear.x)) %>% 
  mutate(reference.x = ifelse(ma_id == "D652", reference.y, reference.x)) %>% 
  select(-study_pubyear.y, - reference.y, - ma_id_study_id) %>%
```

### 5.5. Assign land cover map year

```{r 55}

df <- 
  df %>%
  mutate(landcover_map_year = case_when(
    harvest_year_by_median >= 2000 & harvest_year_by_median <= 2022 ~ harvest_year_by_median,
    harvest_year_by_median < 1975 ~ NA_integer_,
    harvest_year_by_median >= 1975 & harvest_year_by_median <= 1987 ~ 1985,
    harvest_year_by_median >= 1988 & harvest_year_by_median <= 1992 ~ 1990,
    harvest_year_by_median >= 1993 & harvest_year_by_median <= 1997 ~ 1995,
    harvest_year_by_median > 1997 & harvest_year_by_median <= 2000 ~ 2000,
    TRUE ~ NA_integer_  # default case if none of the above conditions match
  ))


```

```{r 61}
df$yield_unit <-  as.factor(df$yield_unit)

# We only handle "convertable" units. 
# those that indicate a yield weight per area.

df <- 
  df %>% 
  mutate(
    yield_control_kgha = case_when(
      yield_unit == "Mg/ha" ~ yield_control*1000, 
      yield_unit == "Mg/ha dry matter" ~ yield_control*1000, 
      yield_unit == "kg/ha" ~ yield_control, 
      yield_unit == "kg/ha (cattle)" ~ yield_control, 
      yield_unit == "kg/hm-2" ~ yield_control*10, 
      yield_unit == "t/ha" ~ yield_control*1000, 
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
      
    ),
    yield_treatment_kgha = case_when(
      yield_unit == "Mg/ha" ~ yield_treatment*1000, 
      yield_unit == "Mg/ha dry matter" ~ yield_treatment*1000, 
      yield_unit == "kg/ha" ~ yield_treatment, 
      yield_unit == "kg/ha (cattle)" ~ yield_treatment, 
      yield_unit == "kg/hm-2" ~ yield_treatment*10, 
      yield_unit == "t/ha" ~ yield_treatment*1000, 
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
      
    )
  )
```

-   so there should be yield for every point

-   and the publication and the landcover map should always be present

-   both control and treatment should be present

-   the units should be present

-   the treatment should be present

## (D) Fix 0 edge issues

There is an issue that some land-cover specifications have 0 edge length.
The reason is unknown.

```{r ID1 0 edge graphs}
data_edgelength_zero <- 
data %>% 
  filter(edgelength_m == 0) %>% 
  select(measurement_id, class,buffer_radius_m, area_m2, edgelength_m) %>% 
  filter(area_m2 != 0) %>% 
  mutate(class = as.factor(class))


## ATTENTION! 
## I exclude class 0 because those are NA areas, and no wonder they have no edge. 
## Though those are the most cases of edge = 0 and area != 0 
data_edgelength_zero %>% 
  group_by(class) %>%
  filter(class != 0) %>%
  summarise(sum_area = sum(area_m2), count = n()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(class), y = sum_area)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), vjust = -0.5) +
  labs(title = "Total Area (m²) Within Classes and Number of 
       zero-edge-Occurrences \nas Bar Label ",
       x = "Class",
       y = "Area (m²)") +
  theme_minimal()

```

There are in total 56 observations that have an area but dont have an edge.

Since we don't know the reasoin we simply fix it.
The fix is that we assume a circular area of that land-cover class and that it is to 100% in the radius.

```{r ID2 fix the zero edge length}

selection<-which(data$edgelength_m==0) 
# calculates from the area the radius of a circle with that area and then 
#computes from the radius the perimeter
data$edgelength_m[selection]<-(sqrt(data$area_m2[selection])) * 2 

rm(selection)

# short check:
x <- data %>% 
  filter(edgelength_m == 0) %>% 
  filter(area_m2 != 0)

# It worked!
```

## (E) check whether yield data is realistic

```{r IE1 check yield data}

hist(data$yield_treatment_kgha)
summary(data$yield_treatment_kgha)

# Alfred uses the following lines to identify the crops that have an 
# inappropriately high yield 
unique(data$crop_type_grouped_small[which(data$yield_treatment_kgha>10^7)])
unique(data$crop_type_grouped_big[which(data$yield_treatment_kgha>10^7)])

# it is also important to check what kind of units are reported 
unique(data$yield_unit[which(data$yield_treatment_kgha>10^7)])

```

@Alfred's comment: this seems to be a bit odd - a very good corn yield per ha is e.g. 13 tons.
So, that fits with the median (6000 kg).
However, we have here a lot of yields that are 10000 tons and higher.
That cannot be right.
We should look into this closer!
One possibility could be that this is the whole biomass and not the corn yield, but that would still weird somehow to report this.

@Elizaveta's comment: Since we do not want to dive into primary literature, lets remove the outliers.
The highest possible maximum for maize yield in controlled conditions is 83.3 t/ha.
<https://www-archiv.fdm.uni-hamburg.de/b-online/library/maize/www.ag.iastate.edu/departments/agronomy/yield.html#>:\~:text=When%20maximizing%20these%20factors%20to,(83.3%20t%2Fha).

83.3 t/ha is 83000 kg/ha.
So let's remove any observation that surpass 100.000 kg/ha

```{r IE2 remove the yield outliers}
data <- 
data %>% 
  mutate(yield_control_kgha = case_when(
      yield_control_kgha > 100000 ~ NA_real_,
    TRUE ~ yield_control_kgha
  )) %>% 
    mutate(yield_treatment_kgha = case_when(
      yield_treatment_kgha > 100000 ~ NA_real_,
    TRUE ~ yield_treatment_kgha
  )) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(yield_control_kgha)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(yield_treatment_kgha))


x <- data %>% select(measurement_id) %>% unique()
hist(data$yield_treatment_kgha)
summary(data$yield_treatment_kgha)

```

In the number of observations we went down to 7429 unique measurements.

@Alfreds comment: There are some data that show a quite high change in values - so either an increase by more than 150% or a shrinkage of the yield in the treatment to less than a quarter of what the original yield was.
This seems extreme - can we trust this?
We should probably also double check?

```{r IE3 high change in yield contr/treatm                  }
# @Elizaveta: I rewrote Alfred's code (the next 2 lines) below

#x<-data$yield_treatment_kgha/ data$yield_control_kgha
#x[which(x> 2.5 | x<0.25)]

data %>% 
  mutate(coef = yield_treatment_kgha/ data$yield_control_kgha) %>% 
  filter(coef %in% (0.25:2.5)) %>% 
  select(-(class:perimeter_to_area)) %>% 
  unique() %>% 
  select(1:5, yield_control_kgha, yield_treatment_kgha)
```

There are only 3 unique measurements with a relatively high change in yield values between control and treatment.

```{r IID average replicates that share location and year Elizavetas}
means <- 
  data.mod.2 %>%
  group_by(landcover_map_year, treatment, Lat_long, crop_type) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_yield_control_kgha = mean(yield_control_kgha, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_yield_treatment_kgha = mean(yield_treatment_kgha, na.rm = TRUE),
    yield_SD_control = sqrt(sum(yield_SD_control_kgha^2)),
    yield_SD_treatment = sqrt(sum(yield_SD_treatment_kgha^2)),
    replicates_control_summed = sum(control_replicates),
    replicates_treatment_summed = sum(treatment_replicates),
    n_aggregated = length(control_replicates)
  ) %>% 
  ungroup()
```

## (E) Add additional columns to aggregated data

Alfred's comment: add remaining data to the average data.
It should be okay to pull in things that have the same latidude-longitude combination and the same land-cover map-year.


```{r IIE joins means with original properties}
means<-cbind(means, data.mod.2[match(paste0(means$Lat_long, 
                                            means$landcover_map_year, means$treatment,
                                            means$crop_type),
                                     paste0(data.mod.2$Lat_long, 
                                            data.mod.2$landcover_map_year, 
                                            data.mod.2$treatment,
                                            data.mod.2$crop_type)),
                               c(1:8,11:12,21:36,41:ncol(data.mod.2))])

# Now landcover_map_year and Lat_long are duplicated 
# lets remove the duplicates of these columns.
means <- means[, -c(37)]
means <- means[, -c(469)] 
 
data.mod.2$reference[data.mod.2$reference=='']<-NA
length(which(is.na(data.mod.2$reference)))/nrow(data.mod.2)


# compute the log-response ratio
means$logrr.yi <- log10(means$mean_yield_control_kgha/means$mean_yield_treatment_kgha)

```

Some references are given in the title or author year columns.
Maybe it makes sense to unite them, because the proportion calculated before is not representative.

## (F) create the inert land-cover

There is an **important change** :

-   Alfred defined inert.land.class.cod as natural habitats, so that inert = 1 - inert.land.class.cod.
    However, all classes are already included in the land cover class table, so it doesnt make much sense in my opinion.
    So here inert.land.class.cod is defined as **non-natural land classes** (bare surfaces and snow)

-   and noninert.land.class.code are all non-inert.

```{r IIIF 1 create the inert land cover}
# (i) get the classes which need to be included and create their col-names
# inert.land.class.code are land cover classes that are build or are snow
inert.land.class.code<-landcover.meta$Class.Code[which(
  landcover.meta$Bigger.CLass=='Bare Surfaces'| 
  landcover.meta$Class.Description.by.ESA=='Permanent ice and snow')]

noninert.land.class.code<-landcover.meta$Class.Code[-which(
  landcover.meta$Bigger.CLass=='Bare Surfaces'| 
  landcover.meta$Class.Description.by.ESA=='Permanent ice and snow')]
```

Comment to the following code section: The urban areas and other built environments ARE included in the land cover classes.
They are called "Impervious surfaces" by teh ESA Classification, have the code 190 and "Bare Surfaces" in Bigger.CLass.

```{r IIIF 2 create the inert land cover}
# Here Elizaveta made changes. Because urban and built areas are included in the bare surfaces there is no need no substract the non inert from 1 as alfred did before. 
names<-c(paste0('proportion_',inert.land.class.code,'_1000'))
reg.data$inert.1000<- rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names))], na.rm = T)

# (iii) repeat that for the 2 and 5km radii
names<-c(paste0('proportion_',inert.land.class.code,'_2500'))
reg.data$inert.2500<- rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names))], na.rm = T)

names<-c(paste0('proportion_',inert.land.class.code,'_5000'))
reg.data$inert.5000<- rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names))], na.rm = T)

# looks good, but we have some very high inert values...
plot(reg.data$inert.1000, reg.data$inert.2500)
plot(reg.data$inert.1000, reg.data$inert.5000)
plot(reg.data$inert.2500, reg.data$inert.5000)


which(reg.data$inert.1000>0.8) # maybe check these points once more? 


```

```{r IIIF 3 look up the points with big urban areas}
names<-c(paste0('proportion_',inert.land.class.code,'_1000'))

means %>% 
  select(measurement_id, country_new, crop_type_grouped_small, treatment, contains("proportion_"), contains("_1000")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  filter((sum(c_across(names), na.rm = TRUE)) > 0.8) %>%
  select(measurement_id) %>% 
  unique()

measurement_ids_biginertproportion <- 
means %>% 
  select(measurement_id, country_new, crop_type_grouped_small, treatment, contains("proportion_"), contains("_1000")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  filter((sum(c_across(names), na.rm = TRUE)) > 0.8) %>%
```

## (F.3) create the  inert area vs perimeter data

```{r IIIB inert area vs perimeter data }
inert.land.class.code<-landcover.meta$Class.Code[which(
  landcover.meta$Bigger.CLass=='Bare Surfaces'| 
  landcover.meta$Class.Description.by.ESA=='Permanent ice and snow')]


# (i) create the column names
names<-c(paste0('area_m2_',inert.land.class.code,'_1000'))
names.per<-c(paste0('edgelength_m_',inert.land.class.code,'_1000'))

# (ii) create the variable
reg.data$inert.peri.area.ratio.1000 <-
  rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names.per))], na.rm = T) /
  rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names))], na.rm = T) # unit: m/m2

# (iii) repeat that for the 2 and 5km radii
 names<-c(paste0('area_m2_',inert.land.class.code,'_2500'))
 names.per<-c(paste0('edgelength_m_',inert.land.class.code,'_2500'))
 reg.data$inert.peri.area.ratio.2500 <-
   rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names.per))], na.rm = T) /
 rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names))], na.rm = T) # unit: m/m2

names<-c(paste0('area_m2_',inert.land.class.code,'_5000'))
names.per<-c(paste0('edgelength_m_',inert.land.class.code,'_5000'))
reg.data$inert.peri.area.ratio.5000 <-
  rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names.per))], na.rm = T) /
  rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names))], na.rm = T) # unit: m/m2

# x<-rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names))], na.rm = T)
# y<-rowSums(means[,which(is.element(col.names,names.per))], na.rm = T)
# 
# which(x==0); which(y==0) 

```


## (H) create the shannon index

```{r IIIH create shannon index}
# (i) define the variables that need to be included
names<-c(paste0('area_m2_',noninert.land.class.code,'_1000')) 
# noninert.land.class.code - contains all non inert land-cover types - non built and non snow

# (ii) create the data frame for the analysis
shannon.df<-means[,which(is.element(col.names,names))]
shannon.df$inert<- reg.data$inert.1000

# (iii) replace NAs with 0s
for(i in 1:ncol(shannon.df)){shannon.df[which(is.na(shannon.df[,i])) , i]<-0}

# (iv) calculate the shannon diversity
library(vegan) # 'species' need to be the columns
reg.data$shannon.1000<-diversity(shannon.df, index = "shannon")

# (v) repeat for the other two radii
names<-c(paste0('area_m2_',noninert.land.class.code,'_2500'))
shannon.df<-means[,which(is.element(col.names,names))]
shannon.df$inert<- reg.data$inert.2500
for(i in 1:ncol(shannon.df)){shannon.df[which(is.na(shannon.df[,i])) , i]<-0}
reg.data$shannon.2500<-diversity(shannon.df, index = "shannon")

names<-c(paste0('area_m2_',noninert.land.class.code,'_5000'))
shannon.df<-means[,which(is.element(col.names,names))]
shannon.df$inert<- reg.data$inert.5000
for(i in 1:ncol(shannon.df)){shannon.df[which(is.na(shannon.df[,i])) , i]<-0}
reg.data$shannon.5000<-diversity(shannon.df, index = "shannon")

```

## (G) create the simpsons evenness

```{r IIIH create simpsons evennes index}
# (i) Define the variables that need to be included
names <- c(paste0('area_m2_', noninert.land.class.code, '_1000')) 
# `noninert.land.class.code` contains all non-inert land-cover types (non-built and non-snow)

# (ii) Create the data frame for the analysis
simpson.df <- means[, which(is.element(col.names, names))]
simpson.df$inert <- reg.data$inert.1000

# (iii) Replace NAs with 0s
for (i in 1:ncol(simpson.df)) {
  simpson.df[which(is.na(simpson.df[, i])), i] <- 0
}

# (iv) Calculate Simpson's Evenness

reg.data$simpsonsevenness.1000 <- diversity(simpson.df, index = "inv")

# (v) Repeat for the other two radii
names <- c(paste0('area_m2_', noninert.land.class.code, '_2500'))
simpson.df <- means[, which(is.element(col.names, names))]
simpson.df$inert <- reg.data$inert.2500
for (i in 1:ncol(simpson.df)) {
  simpson.df[which(is.na(simpson.df[, i])), i] <- 0
}
reg.data$simpsonsevenness.2500 <- diversity(simpson.df, index = "inv")

names <- c(paste0('area_m2_', noninert.land.class.code, '_5000'))
simpson.df <- means[, which(is.element(col.names, names))]
simpson.df$inert <- reg.data$inert.5000
for (i in 1:ncol(simpson.df)) {
  simpson.df[which(is.na(simpson.df[, i])), i] <- 0
}
reg.data$simpsonsevenness.5000 <- diversity(simpson.df, index = "inv")

```
